Developer Notes:
Mutant College is an adult visual novel based on multiple-choice decisions.
Set in a universe quite similar to our own, where 0.003 percent of the population has experienced an evolutionary leap, there are so-called Mutants, human beings endowed with exceptional and extravagant powers that the scientific community has not yet fully understood all aspects of.
The protagonist discovers late in life that he, too, has this kind of mutation; the Ministry of Mutant Management offers him the opportunity to attend Mutant College, a college where mutants are trained to become the heroes of the world, ready to defend the world from threats and catastrophes.
The protagonist in this fantastic and unexpected adventure will have the opportunity to get to know and form bonds with his fellow college students.
You will gain fame and respect among the superheroes on campus.
Features (Full Version):
6000 Full HD Images
100 Full HD Animations
100,000 Words
Multiple Choices
Music & Sound Effects
You Can Decide the Name Of the Character
Ren'py Engine



Jean (from the left), Beth, Claire, Denise, and Ella will be your trusted friends right from the start. With them, you’ll share so much. At Mutant College, you’ll have the chance to get to know multiple girls at once and experience great adventures together. The sandbox feature integrated into the game will help you navigate through the campus and the city map.



The college girls won’t be the only ones bringing you thrilling adventures. Professor Katerina Wallet will be more than just a teacher. Lisa Ward, who runs the campus restaurant, might not be entirely faithful to her husband and may even prefer the company of a brilliant student. Psychologist Lucy Carter will need more than a little “special counseling” herself, while mutant scientist Rebecca… well, Rebecca is just Rebecca.



As in any respectable university, Mutant College also has characters of questionable morality. Led by the stunning and powerful Kira Allen, known as Andromeda, we have the Titanium Dragons. These four alluring girls are among the most powerful mutants on campus. Dating them won’t be easy—you’ll first have to prove your worth as a hero. However, once you get to know them better, you’ll realize that beneath their armor of bravado and power lie hidden vulnerabilities, ambitions, and deep desires.

ye gonna be real, i used to be all about the "dating sim" point & click, simulation, freeroam/sandbox style games. After playing through quite a few of them I realize I'd MUCH rather play a kinetic novel now lol. Most of them are grindy-lost simulators that tend to churn out way too many scenes in different orders based on the player which then leads to you accidentally spoiling certain things without even meaning to, because theres an expected order of events or a lack of a lockout until X point. It's also time consuming and leads you around with a dollar bill on a fishing line.

I like novels with choices (ie: Karlsson gambit where choices actually have a formula of code behind them to determine several values to make certain outcomes possible) but understandably they're a pain to set all the flags for and all the different scenes, branching paths etc but we dont see many of those, lately its been alot of sandbox/point and clicks and they've just been rough in the grind aspect :/ Also you just get to the point where you make the dev tell you every single step from that point on. Another example, I love A House in the Rift, but if it was a kinetic novel it wouldnt have really changed much for me, because i just follow everything the journal tells me anyway

Here are some variables that I found useful that you can set in the console to bypass the grind:

varMindPoint = 3
varKiPoint = 3
varForcePoint = 3
Set these values to 3 to get Rebecca to add an Evolution point; not needed with the value below unless you are like me and like visiting Rebecca .


varMoney (money for dates, you can be the Elon Musk of this world)
varReputation (for the leaderboard rankings)
varEvolution (to open a slot in the statistics page)

I don't know if there are any game triggers in the code that when you get to a particular level that an event happens. I have a hard time reading the code since its in Italian for the UI prompts and dialog, but after playing through I investigated the images folder and don't think I missed anything by bumping up the tiers. MC seems to be maxed out at 500 reputation points so going above that is not advisable as it could cause some weirdness if later on that becomes a factor.
